title.narrative: Strengthening Women-Owned Business Ecosystem and Women Economic Empowerment in Key Value Chains in Ethiopia

description.narrative: This action aims to strengthen the women-owned business ecosystem and women's economic empowerment in key value chains in Ethiopia, fostering decent job creation, socio-economic resilience, and inclusion through improved entrepreneurial ecosystems and greater access to finance. This action will also build upon and benefit from Global Gateway investments in Ethiopia and the 360-degree approach, leaving the scope at national level, with focus on Amhara, Oromia and South Ethiopia regions which together host more than 80% of the IDPs (excluding Tigray). The action will allow to produce commodities which feed the export and industrial development and to strengthen cooperation with EU MS private sector in key agri-value chains, including, but not exhaustive, horticulture, coffee, leather, and non-agri-value chains such as handicraft, etc. It will also contribute to strengthening the local economy, job creation and markets aligned with the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Investing in Young Businesses in Africa.Specifically, the action will cover four three inter-related components identified here as Specific Objectives:1.Enhance the skills and business performance of women from women-headed households, with particular regards to IDPs, IDP returnees, ex-combatants, and returning migrants; women-and-youth-led MSMEs tailored to their specific needs; and start-ups through entrepreneurship trainings and business support, collaborating with ecosystem actors like chambers of commerce, private sector organizations, networks, accelerators, and financial institutions;2.Increase flow of financing and improve access to finance for women-headed households (in particular IDPs, IDP returnees ex-combatants, and returning migrants); women-and-youth-led MSMEs; and start-ups to stimulate business growth and sustainability; 3.Strengthen supply chain management (SCM) of women-and-youth-led enterprises, enabling their genuine participation in key value chains, including but not exhaustive horticulture, coffee, leather and handicraft, and ensuring their competition effectively in the local and national market.
